newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian consortium signs Sabah power deal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian consortium signs Sabah power deal.

text.p: A consortium led by Time Engineering Bhd on Thursday signed a power purchase agreement to supply electricity in eastern Sabah state.
Under the agreement, the consortium, Powertron Resources Sdn Bhd, will sell electricity generated by its 132-megawatt power plant to Sabah Electricity Board at 14.7 cents a unit for 21 years.
The plant was expected to be operational by April 1998 and the project was estimated to cost 345 million ringgit, a Powertron statement said.
The consortium announced the agreement at a signing ceremony here on Thursday.
Powertron was awarded the project by the government on a build-own-operate basis.
Time Engineering holds a 40 percent stake in the consortium, while the other partners are EPE Power Corp Bhd (30 percent), Sabah Energy Corp (20 percent) and Aras Setia Sdn Bhd (10 percent).
